analysis:
Reviewed scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py, an offline unittest that parses .github/workflows/ci.yml and the provider-ci-build composite action. It is a test-only file with no runtime provider, coordinator, key or cache code, so no threat-model assets (A-001..A-019) or trust boundaries (TB-002/003/007/009/011) are changed directly.

Head additions (lines 155-187) introduce CI constants and helpers: pinned action SHAs for checkout and cache, SAVE_POLICY, a git-fsck check on a cached .git, sparse patterns, and work_steps. The cache-save policy (head 158-162) asserts that only pushes to master or dev save caches. The later tests (the head ranges beyond the supplied excerpt, ~787-990) are not visible to me, so I could not confirm what they assert. The visible portion tightens supply-chain hygiene: pinned action SHAs, no continue-on-error, no secrets in provider jobs (head 729-730 in the base-numbered excerpt), and no Rust or backend caches. This reduces CI cache-poisoning exposure, which is indirect to the T-034/T-013 artifact integrity concerns.

The tests still assert that the native gates (MiMo, paged KV, prefix-cache retention such as CBv2NativeHistoricalRetentionTests) are retained and non-skipping. This matters for T-041 prefix-cache regression coverage. I saw no removed assertions that weaken coverage. The base-side deletions (e.g., the SDK condition lines) are not fully visible. The patch excerpt is incomplete, and head lines past 468 were not supplied, so coverage of the remainder is limited.

Remaining question for integration: confirm that the actual ci.yml and action.yml changes (not in this batch) match the SAVE_POLICY and pinned-SHA assertions, and that the cache-key and restore-keys behavior cannot let a pull request poison a master cache. No concrete security regression is identified in the supplied lines.
